hook.line: A game of Hex can never end in a draw: once the board is full, one side is always connected.
hook.say: Welcome to the history of connection games!

ch.say: Two people dreamed up the same game separately.
p: In 1942 the Danish poet and mathematician Piet Hein published it in a newspaper.
Around 1948 John Nash at Princeton invented it independently, and it became a hit among mathematicians.
st: Piet Hein publishes it in Politiken
Nash invents it independently at Princeton
Parker Brothers sells it as Hex
AIs solve small boards; tournaments run

ch.say: It is tied to a theorem of mathematics.
tl: The no-draw property shown equivalent to a mathematical theorem
Computers solve small boards one after another

ch.say: Red links top and bottom, blue links left and right.
ch.cap: A rhombus board: connect your two sides to win
p: Just take turns placing stones on hexagonal cells.
Blocking your rival’s path builds your own — so there can be no draws.

ch.say: A Nobel-winning scientist played it too.
items: Linked to the Brouwer fixed-point theorem
